source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

mx.teacher_note: primitive triple is settled by running 'Recognize that multiplying every entry of a Baudhāyana triple by the': If a² + b² = c², then for any positive integer k, (ka)² + (kb)² = (kc)², so (ka, kb, kc) — on the item about Distinguish primitive Baudhāyana triples from scaled.

intelligence.enrichment: A Baudhāyana triple is primitive when its three entries have no common factor greater than 1; a non-primitive triple can be reduced by dividing all entries by a common factor.
